learn.pulse.p1: Each heartbeat pushes a little more blood into your fingertip. For a moment the fingertip is slightly darker, then lighter again.
learn.pulse.p2: The flash shines through your finger, and the rear camera watches that rhythm of light and dark. Lumen counts the beats and measures the time between them.
learn.pulse.p3: Moving, pressing too hard, and cold fingers all blur the signal. When the signal is not clean, Lumen asks you to retake the reading instead of guessing.
learn.afib.p1: Atrial fibrillation (AFib) is a heart rhythm where the beats come at uneven times. It is often silent, so many people never notice it.
learn.afib.p2: AFib raises the risk of stroke about five-fold. That is why finding it early matters, and why doctors have treatments for it.
learn.afib.p3: When irregular readings repeat within a day, Lumen says "possible AFib". That is a reason to share your report with a doctor, not a diagnosis. Only a doctor can confirm it, usually with an ECG.
learn.afib.p4: One irregular reading is usually just a reason to retake. Sit still, retake, and if it repeats, see a doctor.
learn.rhythm.p1: Lumen measures the time between beats. A steady rhythm has even gaps. An irregular rhythm has gaps that jump around.
learn.rhythm.p2: Several things besides AFib can make the gaps uneven, such as movement, a loose fingertip, and extra beats. Extra beats are common.
learn.rhythm.p3: Lumen cannot tell extra beats from AFib, but a doctor can. If an irregular message repeats, bring your report to a doctor.
learn.stroke.intro: A stroke is an emergency. Learn the signs, and act even if they pass quickly.
learn.stroke.balance: Sudden loss of balance or dizziness.
learn.stroke.eyes: Sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes.
learn.stroke.face: One side of the face droops when smiling.
learn.stroke.arm: One arm is weak or numb.
learn.stroke.speech: Slurred words or trouble finding them.
learn.stroke.time: Call 911 right away, and note when the signs began.
learn.diabetes.p1: Over time, diabetes can change blood vessels, and that can change the shape of the pulse wave seen in a fingertip.
learn.diabetes.p2: Lumen can look for a pulse shape that research has linked to diabetes. This is not a diabetes test. Age, cold hands, and some medicines also change the pulse shape.
learn.diabetes.p3: Only a blood test can tell. If Lumen shows this pattern on repeat readings, ask a doctor or clinic for an A1c blood test.
learn.hrv.p1: Heart rate variability (HRV) is how much the time between beats changes from one beat to the next. A healthy heart does not tick like a metronome.
learn.hrv.p2: A higher, steadier HRV usually goes with better recovery from stress, hard exercise, and poor sleep. HRV tends to drop when you are tired or run down.
learn.hrv.p3: HRV is personal. Compare your own readings over weeks, at the same time of day, rather than comparing yourself with other people.
learn.hrv.p4: See "How accurate is Lumen?" in Settings for how well its HRV matches a chest strap.
learn.limits.p1: Lumen watches light change in a fingertip. That is enough for pulse, rhythm, HRV, and breathing rate, but not for everything.
learn.limits.p2: It cannot measure blood pressure, blood oxygen, or artery age, and it cannot tell whether a heart attack is happening.
learn.limits.p3: Chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath need emergency care, not a Lumen reading. Call 911.
learn.limits.p4: Saying plainly what Lumen cannot do is part of being honest about what it can.
learn.doctor.p1: Lumen is a screening prototype. It can suggest a visit, but it never gives a diagnosis.
learn.doctor.p2: Call 911 right away for chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, or stroke signs (BE FAST).
learn.doctor.p3: Book a visit if an irregular-rhythm message repeats on different days, if your resting heart rate stays unusually high or low, or if your heart often races or skips.
learn.doctor.p4: Bring your Lumen report. It lists your readings and how reliable each one was.
learn.doctor.p5: If cost is a worry, use the health-center finder at the bottom of the Learn tab.

dr.notInScore: Not part of the risk score.
dr.demoRow: Example reading. Your own answers are not shown here.
dr.pulseNeedsFull: The pulse pattern preview needs a Full Scan.
quality.sheetTitle: Why this reading is lower quality
quality.lowFps: Your camera films at {{fps}} frames per second; beat timing is less precise than at {{want}}
quality.modelFallback: A simpler rhythm method was used
quality.quickMode: Quick Check is short (30 s); a Full Scan is more reliable
quality.contact: Only {{pct}}% of the scan was clean (finger contact or movement)
quality.sqiFlagged: The signal-quality check flagged {{windows}} of {{total}} parts of this reading
quality.sqiUnscored: The signal-quality check skipped {{seconds}} seconds of this reading
quality.rhythmUnjudged: HRV was worked out without checking that the rhythm was regular
quality.fewBeats: Only {{beats}} beats were measured (we like {{want}} or more)
quality.fewWindows: Only {{windows}} of {{want}} steady stretches were usable
quality.betterTitle: How to get a better reading
quality.tipFlat: Keep your finger flat across the lens and flash.
quality.tipStill: Hold still and rest your elbows on a table.
quality.tipFull: Take a Full Scan for the most reliable result.
quality.confirmAf: Confirm with a Full Scan; see a doctor if it repeats.
quality.missingShort: This scan was too short for this check.
quality.missingBeats: Too few beats were measured for this check.
quality.missingWindows: Too few steady stretches for this check.
quality.estimatesDisagree: The three breathing signals disagreed, so one of them is shown
quality.phoneTier: This phone is rated {{tier}}; this check is made for {{want}} phones
quality.missingNoRhythm: HRV needs a rhythm result first, and there was none.
quality.missingNotSinus: HRV is not shown when the rhythm was not clearly regular.
trends.rhythmHint: Each dot is one beat compared with the next. Tap a map to see why.
learn.beFastLabel: Stroke warning signs: BE FAST. Opens the Get help now screen.
learn.beFastBody: If you see any of these signs, call 911 right away, even if they pass quickly.
phoneRating.unlocks: Lumen can check on this phone
learn.rhythm.barsCaption: Each bar is one gap between beats. Taller bar, longer gap.
learn.rhythm.heroLabel: A fingertip covers the rear camera and flash. 1, flash lights the fingertip. 2, blood changes the light. 3, camera sees the change.
learn.rhythm.stripLabel: What the camera sees: the fingertip turns darker at each beat and lighter between beats
learn.rhythm.traceLabel: The pulse trace Lumen builds from that light, with a dot on each beat and the time between two beats marked
learn.rhythm.heroCaption: The flash shines through your finger, and the rear camera watches that rhythm of light and dark. Lumen counts the beats and measures the time between them.
learn.rhythm.gapsLabel: Steady rhythm: gaps of about 920 to 950 ms, so the bars are even. Irregular rhythm: gaps from 590 to 1180 ms, so the bars jump up and down.
learn.rhythm.mapHint: Each dot is one beat compared with the next
learn.rhythm.mapsLabel: Two rhythm maps. Steady: a narrow streak along the line. Irregular: a round, scattered cloud.
learn.rhythm.extraLabel: Rhythm map with extra beats: a streak plus dots off to the side. Rhythm map of an irregular rhythm: a scattered cloud. Both can look irregular to this check.
profile.name: Name (optional)
placement.tipPosture: Elbows on a table, phone at chest height
placement.tipWarm: Warm hands help. Rub them together if they feel cold.
reminders.previewNote: This is all your lock screen will ever show.
howToSit.title: How to sit
howToSit.subtitle: Steady arms and warm hands give the cleanest pulse.
howToSit.warm: Hands warm (rub them if they feel cold)
profile.nameHelp: Lumen uses it to greet you on Home. You can leave it blank.
phoneCheck.dialLabel: {{points}} of {{total}} capability points so far. Frame timing is measured in practice.
phoneCheck.progressSettled: {{done}} of {{total}} checked. Frame timing is measured during practice.
phoneCheck.timingMeterLabel: {{name}}: not measured yet, up to {{max}} points
results.breathLabel: Breathing {{value}} breaths per minute, typical resting range {{low}} to {{high}}
report.everyReading: Every reading gets a report. A lower-quality reading is marked here with a quality note. An inconclusive one lists only what was measured and why it fell short.
report.mapNote: Each dot is one beat compared with the next.
why.readMapTitle: How to read your rhythm map
why.guideExtraNote: Streak plus dots off to the side
why.tachoCaption: Every gap in the reading, in order.
learn.ch1.heroLabel: Side view: a fingertip rests on the rear camera and flash. Light from the flash scatters through the fingertip and its blood vessel, then returns to the camera.
learn.ch1.heroCaption: Your fingertip covers both the flash and the rear camera.
learn.ch1.pairLabel: Two fingertips. At a beat the vessel holds a little more blood and the fingertip looks darker. Between beats it looks lighter again.
learn.ch1.fromLightSub: What Lumen builds from the camera
learn.ch1.traceLabel: Camera frames that are darker at each beat and lighter between, and the pulse trace Lumen builds from that light, with a dot on each beat and the time between two beats marked
learn.ch1.compareLabel: A clean signal has clear beats, so Lumen measures. A blurry signal has no clear beats, so Lumen asks for a retake.
learn.ch3.heroLabel: Two pulse traces. Regular rhythm: beats at even times. AFib: beats at uneven times.
learn.ch3.heroCaption: In a regular rhythm the beats come at even times. In AFib they come at uneven times.
learn.ch3.silentLabel: A person feels fine while their beats come at uneven times. AFib is often silent.
learn.ch3.riskLabel: Stroke risk compared: with AFib the bar is about five times as long as without AFib
learn.ch3.riskNote: Shows the relative rise, not your own risk.
learn.ch3.dayLabel: Three readings in one day: the morning reading is regular, the midday and evening readings are irregular
learn.ch3.stepRepeat: Irregular readings repeat within a day
learn.ch3.stepShare: Share your report with a doctor
learn.ch3.stepConfirm: Only a doctor can confirm it, usually with an ECG
learn.ch3.notDiagnosis: A reason to see a doctor, not a diagnosis
learn.ch3.repeatsSee: If it repeats, see a doctor
learn.ch4.artEyes: An eye with half of the view dark
learn.ch4.artFace: A smile that droops on one side
learn.ch4.artArm: Both arms raised, one drifting down
learn.ch4.artSpeech: A speech bubble with slurred words
learn.ch4.artTime: A clock and a phone dialing 911
learn.ch4.rowLabel: BE FAST: Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time to call 911
learn.ch4.listLabel: BE FAST, one letter at a time
learn.diabetes.heroLabel: The pulse wave seen in a fingertip. One beat is magnified to show that each beat has a shape.
learn.diabetes.heroTitle: Pulse wave seen in a fingertip
learn.diabetes.heroCaption: This check looks at the shape of the pulse wave, not only how fast it beats.
learn.diabetes.chainLabel: Over time, diabetes can change blood vessels, and that can change the pulse shape. Two example pulse shapes: one, and a changed one.
learn.diabetes.linkedSub: A shape research has linked to diabetes
learn.diabetes.compareLabel: Lumen compares your pulse shape with a pattern linked to diabetes in research
learn.diabetes.notATest: This is not a diabetes test
learn.diabetes.needsFrames: Needs a phone that films at 60 frames per second.
learn.diabetes.sidesLabel: Lumen compared with a blood test
learn.diabetes.lumenCan: Can show a pulse pattern. Not a diabetes test.
learn.diabetes.a1cOnly: Only a blood test can tell.
learn.diabetes.stepTalk: Talk to a doctor or clinic
learn.diabetes.stepA1c: Ask for an A1c blood test
placement.instructionAndroid: Lay the pad of your finger flat across the flash and the top lens, the main camera of your Galaxy A17.
placement.instructionIos: Lay the pad of your finger flat across the flash and the main lens, the big one at the top left of your iPhone 17 Pro.
placement.figureLabelAndroid: Back of a Samsung Galaxy A17: the fingertip lies flat across the top main lens and the flash beside it.
placement.figureLabelIos: Back of an iPhone 17 Pro: the fingertip lies flat across the main lens at the top left and the flash.
